summary: Checked every registry repo (all 9, excluding loop-engine-state) for open PRs and default-branch CI, one agent per repo in parallel. Seven repos (analytics-service-toolkit, btc-llm-sentiment, kinz-accounting-analysis-20260623-102129, feed-quality-gate, kinz-competitor-intelligence, kinz-margin-guardian-pipeline, kinz-price-bridge) were quiet: no open PRs, main green (except btc-llm-sentiment, see below), nothing to merge or fix. Next.js-SaaS: dependabot PR #95 (@radix-ui/react-select), previously stuck on a mangled '@dependabot rebase' comment, had self-rebased clean with all checks green -- merged (squash). kinz-secure-commerce-hub: found default-branch CI red since 2026-10-01 (pip-audit flagging 13 CVEs in PyJWT==2.13.0, plus a Trivy Security-scans failure); opened PR #73 bumping PyJWT and adding two justified .trivyignore entries for a pip-vendored urllib3, verified both fixes locally, but a third OS-layer CVE (likely CVE-2026-103111 in libpcre2-8-0) could not be confirmed or fixed because this sandbox's container network cannot reach deb.debian.org to build the repo's actual Dockerfile -- PR #73 left open with CI not fully green, main still red. btc-llm-sentiment's main also stayed red and its 5 dependabot PRs stayed open, but that is the already-diagnosed (2026-09-27, 2026-10-01) Docker build / numpy-shap Python-version conflict needing a coordinated, dedicated re-pin -- correctly not re-attempted as a maintenance-scope fix. kinz-margin-guardian-pipeline and kinz-price-bridge visibility re-confirmed still public (recorded private) -- unchanged, owner decision only, flagged again. One subagent (kinz-secure-commerce-hub) briefly triggered a PR-activity subscription on #73 via a tool call; the main session caught and reversed it immediately since this job's rules forbid watching PRs.
errors: kinz-secure-commerce-hub #73: a third Trivy finding (OS package, likely CVE-2026-103111/libpcre2-8-0) is unconfirmed and unfixed -- the sandbox's container network blocks deb.debian.org so the repo's multi-stage Dockerfile cannot be built and re-scanned here. A future run with normal container network access should rebuild the image, re-run Trivy, and either confirm apt-get upgrade already resolves it or add a properly-justified .trivyignore entry.

kinz-secure-commerce-hub #37 and #64: #37 is still genuinely conflicted (real Tailwind v4 migration, not a small fix) and inside the 48h dependabot-rebase cooldown from 2026-10-01, so not re-poked. #64 (httpx) is NOT actually conflicted despite the 2026-10-01 note saying so (mergeable_state is 'unstable', not 'dirty') -- its only failure is the same Security-scans root cause as main; a future run should update its branch once PR #73 (or an equivalent fix) lands on main.

A subagent working in kinz-secure-commerce-hub caused this session to be subscribed to PR activity on #73 (subscription.created event received); unsubscribed immediately on the main session since cloud-maintenance must not watch PRs.
